action.description: What to do. 'attach' opens the live simulator panel for the user — call it BEFORE you build or launch, as soon as the user wants to see the app: on a booted simulator it opens immediately, and otherwise it returns a clear, harmless error (boot or build first, then retry it). Do not skip the early attach because 'launch' also attaches — the panel should be open before the build starts. The panel is the user's view, not a precondition — 'screenshot' and input actions work without it. Skip it only when the user has no interest in watching; 'launch' installs and launches an .app (it also re-attaches, but call 'attach' early rather than relying on that); 'screenshot' returns a PNG of the current screen; 'tap'/'swipe'/'text'/'button' inject input; 'press_key' presses a hardware key 'count' times: return, delete (backspace), an arrow, select_all, undo or redo (a key also hides the on-screen keyboard); 'set_appearance' switches the device to light or dark mode; 'appearance' says which it is in; 'set_keyboard' shows or hides the on-screen keyboard (it appears only while a text field has focus, and 'press_key' and 'text' hide it again); 'rotate' turns the device a quarter turn left or right ('direction'); take a 'screenshot' after it and tap in that screenshot's frame, however it comes back; 'touch_path' performs a single-finger drag along an arbitrary path (eased curves, long-press-then-drag); 'touch2_path' is the two-finger variant for pinch/rotate; 'open_url' opens a deep link; 'detach' closes the panel/stream. NOTE: a 'swipe' or 'touch_path' whose start point is on-screen and within 4pt of an edge performs the OS edge gesture instead of a plain drag — left=back, top=notification shade, bottom=home/app-switcher, right=Control Center (mapped to the current interface orientation). Start more than 4pt from the edge to drag or scroll content near the bezel.

app_path.description: For 'launch': absolute path (no ~) to the built .app bundle (e.g. /Users/me/Library/Developer/Xcode/DerivedData/MyApp-abc123/Build/Products/Debug-iphonesimulator/MyApp.app).

device.description: Simulator name (e.g. 'iPhone 17 Pro') or UDID. Defaults to the simulator already attached, else the first booted one. The first use of a device asks the user for permission.

udid.description: Alias for 'device' (identical semantics: simulator name or UDID). Pass at most one of 'device' / 'udid'.

bundle_id.description: For 'launch': bundle identifier. If omitted, extracted from the .app's Info.plist.

points.description: For 'touch_path': touch path samples in device points. First point is touch-down; last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000 ms; the first sample's is skipped, so send 0 or omit it; at most 30 seconds in all).

points2.description: For 'touch2_path': two-finger path samples in device points. Each sample carries both contacts (x1/y1, x2/y2); first is touch-down, last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000 ms; the first sample's is skipped, so send 0 or omit it; at most 30 seconds in all).

duration.description: Seconds. For 'tap', >0.5 is a long-press. For 'swipe', the gesture duration (default 0.3).

key.description: For 'press_key': the key or edit command to press.

count.description: For 'press_key': how many times to press it, 1 to 20 (default 1).

state.description: For 'set_keyboard': 'show' or 'hide' the on-screen keyboard. For 'set_appearance': 'light' or 'dark'.

url.description: For 'open_url': URL or scheme to open in the simulator.

loading_messages.description: 1–4 loading messages shown to the user while the visual renders, each roughly 5 words long. Write them in the same language the user is using. Use 1 for simple visuals, more for complex ones. If the topic is serious — illness, disease, pandemics, death, grief, war, conflict, poverty, disaster, trauma, abuse, addiction, medical decisions, politically charged subjects, or anything where the reader might be personally affected — keep these BORING: describe what the code is doing in the dullest generic way, no jargon-as-drama, no evocative terms. Pandemic growth model — NOT ['Simulating patient zero', 'Modeling the curve'] (documentary-narrator voice), YES ['Setting up the model', 'Running the calculation']. Cancer timeline — NOT ['Charting the battle ahead'], YES ['Laying out the stages']. If you have to ask whether it's serious, it is. Otherwise, have fun — reach for alliteration, puns, personification, wordplay, whatever lands in that language. Playful examples — revenue chart: ['Bribing bars to stand taller', 'Asking Q4 where it went']; kanban: ['Herding cards into columns', 'Dragging, dropping, not stopping'].

**Why the PR is blocked.** The brief allows a PR "only if every mandatory obligation is proved and every expected/obtained mismatch resolved". Neither condition holds:

- Three mandatory obligations are false under spec v0: O2.b, O2.c and O3.e. All three follow from one specification defect: `transfer` (§63) admits an ownership cycle that breaks §49.8 and §57 (`Access.transfer_breaks_kinv`, `Access.reachable_kinv_false`).
- Two HandlePool obligations, O5.e and O5.f, are false by the non-normative v0.4 annex itself, on nested pools.
- Seven obligations are proved only under hypotheses that are not spec clauses: O3.a, O3.b, O4.c, O4.d, O4.e, O4.j and O5.g.
- All five corpus obligations (O7.a to O7.e) keep expected/obtained mismatches that are still open.

The brief prescribes what to do in that case: commit on the branch, do not push, do not open the PR, and end with this report. Every item is classified in section 1.

import Ern.MemoryModel.Machine

/-!
# Corpus MM2-H on the memory machine (test module, spec v0 Parts II–III, §8–§20)

Test module. It states no semantics: it runs the MM2-H corpus (non-normative validation
material, 17 identifiers, H13 split into H13a and H13b, 18 scenarios) on the relations of
`Ern.MemoryModel.Machine`.

Each case gives a state reached from the empty state, an admissible initial state (§9 ¶9), by an
execution of `ok` steps (`Exec`, §20.3 ¶3), and the outcome of the normative relation at that
state (`ReadStep`, `WriteStep`, `DeallocStep`, `AllocStep`, §20.1), proved by `decide` or by the
machine lemmas. Each `ub` case has a separate `_twin` theorem for the corpus's positive twin.
The docstring of each theorem states the expected verdict from the corpus, the obtained verdict,
and the class (rule "classement" of the corpus: `N2` = memory machine). Where the obtained
verdict differs from the expected one, the docstring says "Mismatch" and the case is kept as
written, not corrected.

Context of every execution (§20.3 ¶1, §20.3 ¶3: explicit context parameters): compatibility is
equality of the presented authority with the recorded token (§17 ¶4); read and write
obligations are the machine's explicit test instances `Witness.obR` and `Witness.obW` (both parts
`True`), except in H14, which needs a false static part.

Open obligations, not declared passed: H10 address formation (§14 ¶4, §19), H13a at language
level (§10 ¶4, §19), H13b (§19).
-/

namespace Ern.Corpus.MM2H

open Ern.MemoryModel.Machine

/-! ## Run builders -/

section Builders

variable {Ty : Type} {C : Nat → Nat → Prop} {R : ReadOblSpec Ty} {W : WriteOblSpec Ty}

/-- An execution extended by one `ok` step at its end is an execution (§20.1 ¶2, §20.3 ¶3). -/
theorem exec_snoc {ops : List (Op Ty)} {op : Op Ty} {s₀ s s' : State}
    (h : Exec C R W ops s₀ s) (hs : Step C R W op s s') : Exec C R W (ops ++ [op]) s₀ s' := by
which receives identity `1` (§13 ¶1, §13 ¶2). -/
abbrev h01 : State := (a8w.dealloc 0).alloc 0 96 8 8 (some 7)

/-- Operations reaching `h01` (§9 ¶11, §16, §17). -/
abbrev h01Ops : List (Op Unit) :=
  [.alloc 0 96 8 8 (some 7), .write (wr 0) () Witness.w₀, .dealloc 0 7, .alloc 0 96 8 8 (some 7)]

/-- `h01` is reached, and the new allocation lies at the old base `96` (§13 ¶2). -/
theorem run_h01 : Run h01Ops h01 ∧ ∃ b, h01.allocs 1 = some b ∧ b.live = true ∧ b.base = 96 :=
  ⟨run_alloc (run_dealloc run_a8w (by decide)) (by decide), _, rfl, rfl, rfl⟩

/-- H01. Free, allocate at the same base, read through the old access. Expected `ub`;
obtained `ub`: the old provenance designates the dead allocation `0` (§12 ¶3, §13 ¶2, §15.1,
§17 ¶3). Class N2. -/
theorem H01 : Run h01Ops h01 ∧ ReadStep ctxR (rd 0) () h01 .ub :=
  ⟨run_h01.1, readStep_of (by decide)⟩

/-- H01 twin as written ("read through the new access"). Expected `ok`; obtained `ub`.
Mismatch, case defect: the new allocation is wholly uninitialized (§10 ¶5), so a read of
length `8` through it violates §15.3. Class N2. -/
theorem H01_twin : Run h01Ops h01 ∧ ReadStep ctxR (rd 1) () h01 .ub :=
  ⟨run_h01.1, readStep_of (by decide)⟩

/-- Variant of the H01 twin, not the corpus's twin: a write through the new access before the
read. Obtained `ok` with the written bytes (§16 ¶2, §16 ¶5). It shows that the `ub` of
`H01_twin` comes from §10 ¶5, not from the address reuse. -/
theorem H01_twin_variant :
    Run (h01Ops ++ [.write (wr 1) () Witness.w₀]) (h01.write (wr 1) Witness.w₀) ∧
    ReadStep ctxR (rd 1) () (h01.write (wr 1) Witness.w₀) (.ok (writtenBytes Witness.w₀ 0 8)) :=
  ⟨run_write run_h01.1 (by decide) trivial trivial, readStep_of (by decide)⟩

/-! ## H02, H03 — deallocation -/

/-- H02. Double deallocation. Expected `ub`; obtained `ub`: the allocation is dead (§17.1,
§17 ¶3). Class N2. -/
theorem H02 : Run [.alloc 0 96 8 8 (some 7), .dealloc 0 7] a8d ∧
    DeallocStep (· = ·) 0 7 a8d .ub :=
  ⟨run_a8d, .ub (by decide)⟩

/-- H02 twin: a single deallocation. Expected `ok`; obtained `ok` (§17.1, §17.2). Class N2. -/
theorem H02_twin : Run [.alloc 0 96 8 8 (some 7)] a8 ∧ DeallocStep (· = ·) 0 7 a8 (.ok a8d) :=
  ⟨run_a8, .ok (by decide)⟩

/-- H03. Deallocation with an authority (`8`) not compatible with the token (`7`) under the
context relation. Expected `ub`; obtained `ub` (§17.2, §17 ¶4, §20.3 ¶3). Class N2. -/
theorem H03 : Run [.alloc 0 96 8 8 (some 7)] a8 ∧ DeallocStep (· = ·) 0 8 a8 .ub :=
  ⟨run_a8, .ub (by decide)⟩

/-- H03 twin: compatible authority `7`. Expected `ok`; obtained `ok` (§17.2). Class N2. -/
theorem H03_twin : Run [.alloc 0 96 8 8 (some 7)] a8 ∧ DeallocStep (· = ·) 0 7 a8 (.ok a8d) :=
  H02_twin

/-! ## H04, H05, H06 — read conditions -/

/-- H04. Read of uninitialized bytes, right after creation. Expected `ub`; obtained `ub`
(§10 ¶5, §15.3). Class N2. -/
theorem H04 : Run [.alloc 0 96 8 8 (some 7)] a8 ∧ ReadStep ctxR (rd 0) () a8 .ub :=
  ⟨run_a8, readStep_of (by decide)⟩

/-- H04 twin: write, then read. Expected `ok`; obtained `ok` with the written bytes (§16 ¶2,
§16 ¶5). Class N2. -/
theorem H04_twin : Run [.alloc 0 96 8 8 (some 7), .write (wr 0) () Witness.w₀] a8w ∧
    ReadStep ctxR (rd 0) () a8w (.ok (writtenBytes Witness.w₀ 0 8)) :=
  ⟨run_a8w, readStep_of (by decide)⟩

/-- H05. Read of `[101, 105)`, one byte past the end `104`. Expected `ub`; obtained `ub`
(§15 ¶1, §15.2). Class N2. -/
theorem H05 : Run [.alloc 0 96 8 8 (some 7), .write (wr 0) () Witness.w₀] a8w ∧
    ReadStep ctxR ⟨101, 0, 4, .read⟩ () a8w .ub :=
  ⟨run_a8w, readStep_of (by decide)⟩

/-- H05 twin: read of `[100, 104)`, ending at the end. Expected `ok`; obtained `ok` with the
written bytes (§15 ¶1, §16 ¶5). Class N2. -/
theorem H05_twin : Run [.alloc 0 96 8 8 (some 7), .write (wr 0) () Witness.w₀] a8w ∧
    ReadStep ctxR ⟨100, 0, 4, .read⟩ () a8w (.ok (writtenBytes Witness.w₀ 4 4)) :=
  ⟨run_a8w, readStep_of (by decide)⟩

/-- Zero-length read access at address `104`, just after the end of `[96, 104)` (§15 ¶3). -/
def rz : Access := ⟨104, 0, 0, .read⟩

/-- H06. Zero-length read just after the end of a dead allocation. Expected `ub`; obtained
`ub` (§15.1, §15 ¶3, §17 ¶3). Class N2. -/
theorem H06 : Run [.alloc 0 96 8 8 (some 7), .dealloc 0 7] a8d ∧ ReadStep ctxR rz () a8d .ub :=
  ⟨run_a8d, readStep_of (by decide)⟩

/-- H06 twin: same access, allocation live. Expected `ok`; obtained `ok` with no bytes: the
spatial condition admits address `b + s` and no initialized byte is required (§15 ¶3).
Class N2. -/
theorem H06_twin : Run [.alloc 0 96 8 8 (some 7)] a8 ∧ ReadStep ctxR rz () a8 (.ok []) :=
  ⟨run_a8, readStep_of (by decide)⟩

/-! ## H07, H08 — creation preconditions -/

/-- H07. Creation of `[100, 108)` in space `0`, overlapping the live `[96, 104)` of the same
space. Expected `ub`; obtained `ub` (§9 ¶3, §9 ¶11). Class N2. -/
theorem H07 : Run [.alloc 0 96 8 8 (some 7)] a8 ∧ AllocStep 0 100 8 4 none a8 .ub :=
  ⟨run_a8, allocStep_ub run_a8 (by decide)⟩

/-- H07 twins: the same creation in another space (`1`), or in space `0` after the
overlapped allocation died. Expected `ok`; obtained `ok` (§9 ¶3, §9 ¶11). Class N2. -/
theorem H07_twin : AllocStep 1 100 8 4 none a8 (.ok (a8.alloc 1 100 8 4 none)) ∧
    Run [.alloc 0 96 8 8 (some 7), .dealloc 0 7] a8d ∧
    AllocStep 0 100 8 4 none a8d (.ok (a8d.alloc 0 100 8 4 none)) :=
  ⟨allocStep_ok run_a8 (by decide), run_a8d, allocStep_ok run_a8d (by decide)⟩

/-- H08. From the empty state (admissible, §9 ¶9): alignment `3`, not a power of two, with
base `96` a multiple of `3`; and base `100` not a multiple of alignment `8`. Expected `ub`;
obtained `ub` for both (§9 ¶4, §9 ¶11). Class N2. -/
theorem H08 : AllocStep 0 96 8 3 none State.empty .ub ∧ AllocStep 0 100 8 8 none State.empty .ub :=
  ⟨allocStep_ub run_empty (by decide), allocStep_ub run_empty (by decide)⟩

/-- H08 twins: valid alignment `4` for each faulty creation. Expected `ok`; obtained `ok`
(§9 ¶4, §9 ¶11). Class N2. -/
theorem H08_twin :
    AllocStep 0 96 8 4 none State.empty (.ok (State.empty.alloc 0 96 8 4 none)) ∧
    AllocStep 0 100 8 4 none State.empty (.ok (State.empty.alloc 0 100 8 4 none)) :=
  ⟨allocStep_ok run_empty (by decide), allocStep_ok run_empty (by decide)⟩

/-! ## H09, H10 — write authority, derivation -/

/-- H09. Write through an access whose elementary authority is `read`. Expected `ub`;
obtained `ub` (§12 ¶4, §16.3). Class N2. -/
theorem H09 : Run [.alloc 0 96 8 8 (some 7)] a8 ∧
    WriteStep ctxW ⟨96, 0, 8, .read⟩ () Witness.w₀ a8 .ub :=
  ⟨run_a8, .ub fun h => absurd h.1 (by decide)⟩

/-- H09 twin: write authority. Expected `ok`; obtained `ok` (§16.3). Class N2. -/
theorem H09_twin : Run [.alloc 0 96 8 8 (some 7)] a8 ∧
    WriteStep ctxW (wr 0) () Witness.w₀ a8 (.ok a8w) :=
  ⟨run_a8, .ok ⟨by decide, trivial, trivial⟩⟩

/-- Source access of H10: write access to `[96, 100)` of allocation `0` (§12 ¶1). -/
def h10src : Access := ⟨96, 0, 4, .write⟩

/-- Access formed outside the source range `[96, 100)` but inside the allocation:
`[100, 104)` (§14 ¶4). -/
def h10out : Access := ⟨100, 0, 4, .write⟩

/-- Access formed outside the source range and outside the allocation: `[104, 108)`
(§14 ¶4). -/
def h10past : Access := ⟨104, 0, 4, .write⟩

/-- Restrictive derivation of `h10src` inside its range: `[98, 100)` (§14 ¶1). -/
def h10in : Access := ⟨98, 0, 2, .write⟩

/-- H10, use of an access formed outside the source range that leaves the allocation.
Expected `ub` for the use; obtained `ub` (§15 ¶1, §16.2). The formation itself has no
transition in the machine and no verdict: open obligation (§14 ¶4, §19), not declared passed.
Class N2. -/
theorem H10 : Run [.alloc 0 96 8 8 (some 7)] a8 ∧ ¬ Derive h10src h10past ∧
    WriteStep ctxW h10past () Witness.w₀ a8 .ub :=
  ⟨run_a8, fun h => absurd h.2.1 (by decide), .ub fun h => absurd h.1 (by decide)⟩

/-- H10, use of an access formed outside the source range but inside the allocation.
Expected `ub`; obtained `ok`. Mismatch, case defect: provenance has allocation granularity in
the machine (§14 ¶2), so only leaving the allocation makes the use `ub` (§16.2); the scenario
does not say which. Class N2. -/
theorem H10_inside : Run [.alloc 0 96 8 8 (some 7)] a8 ∧ ¬ Derive h10src h10out ∧
    WriteStep ctxW h10out () Witness.w₀ a8 (.ok (a8.write h10out Witness.w₀)) :=
  ⟨run_a8, fun h => absurd h.2.1 (by decide), .ok ⟨by decide, trivial, trivial⟩⟩

/-- H10 twin: a restrictive derivation inside the source range, then use. Expected `ok`;
obtained `ok` (§14 ¶1, §16). Class N2. -/
theorem H10_twin : Run [.alloc 0 96 8 8 (some 7)] a8 ∧ Derive h10src h10in ∧
    WriteStep ctxW h10in () Witness.w₀ a8 (.ok (a8.write h10in Witness.w₀)) :=
  ⟨run_a8, ⟨by decide, by decide, rfl, by decide⟩, .ok ⟨by decide, trivial, trivial⟩⟩

/-! ## H11, H12 — read-after-write and non-interference -/

/-- H11. Write `[96, 104)`, read the contained subrange `[98, 101)`. Expected: the written
sub-contents; obtained `ok` with positions `2..4` of the written representation (§16 ¶5).
Class N2. -/
theorem H11 : Run [.alloc 0 96 8 8 (some 7), .write (wr 0) () Witness.w₀] a8w ∧
    ReadStep ctxR ⟨98, 0, 3, .read⟩ () a8w (.ok (writtenBytes Witness.w₀ 2 3)) :=
  ⟨run_a8w, readStep_of (by decide)⟩

/-- Second written representation of H12: byte `170`, no provenance, at every position
(§10 ¶2). -/
def w₁ : Nat → UInt8 × Option Nat := fun _ => (170, none)

/-- State of H12: allocations `0` (`[96, 104)`) and `1` (`[128, 136)`, same space), and
`[96, 100)` written with `Witness.w₀` (§9 ¶3, §16 ¶2). -/
abbrev h12 : State := (a8.alloc 0 128 8 8 none).write ⟨96, 0, 4, .write⟩ Witness.w₀

/-- Operations reaching `h12` (§9 ¶11, §16). -/
abbrev h12Ops : List (Op Unit) :=
  [.alloc 0 96 8 8 (some 7), .alloc 0 128 8 8 none, .write ⟨96, 0, 4, .write⟩ () Witness.w₀]

/-- `h12` is reached (§9 ¶11, §16). -/
theorem run_h12 : Run h12Ops h12 :=
  run_write (run_alloc run_a8 (by decide)) (by decide) trivial trivial

/-- H12. After `h12`, a write of a disjoint range of the same allocation (`[100, 104)`), or a
write of the other allocation, leaves the read of `[96, 100)` unchanged. Expected: contents
unchanged; obtained: the same `ok` bytes before and after each write (§16 ¶3, §16 ¶5).
Class N2. -/
theorem H12 : Run h12Ops h12 ∧
    ReadStep ctxR ⟨96, 0, 4, .read⟩ () h12 (.ok (writtenBytes Witness.w₀ 0 4)) ∧
    Run (h12Ops ++ [.write ⟨100, 0, 4, .write⟩ () w₁]) (h12.write ⟨100, 0, 4, .write⟩ w₁) ∧
    ReadStep ctxR ⟨96, 0, 4, .read⟩ () (h12.write ⟨100, 0, 4, .write⟩ w₁)
      (.ok (writtenBytes Witness.w₀ 0 4)) ∧
    Run (h12Ops ++ [.write ⟨128, 1, 8, .write⟩ () w₁]) (h12.write ⟨128, 1, 8, .write⟩ w₁) ∧
    ReadStep ctxR ⟨96, 0, 4, .read⟩ () (h12.write ⟨128, 1, 8, .write⟩ w₁)
      (.ok (writtenBytes Witness.w₀ 0 4)) :=
  ⟨run_h12, readStep_of (by decide), run_write run_h12 (by decide) trivial trivial,
    readStep_of (by decide), run_write run_h12 (by decide) trivial trivial,
    readStep_of (by decide)⟩

/-! ## H13a, H13b — pointer bytes -/

/-- Representation written as a pointer: byte values of the address `64` (low byte first) and
provenance `0`, the allocation at `64`, on every byte. The byte encoding is a choice of this
test; the provenance comes from the written representation (§10 ¶4, §16 ¶2). -/
def ptrRep : Nat → UInt8 × Option Nat := fun i => (if i = 0 then 64 else 0, some 0)

/-- State of H13a before the copy: allocations `0` (`[64, 72)`), `1` (`[96, 104)`, source)
and `2` (`[128, 136)`, destination); `ptrRep` written over the source (§9 ¶11, §16 ¶2). -/
abbrev h13Src : State :=
  (((State.empty.alloc 0 64 8 8 none).alloc 0 96 8 8 none).alloc 0 128 8 8 none).write
    ⟨96, 1, 8, .write⟩ ptrRep

/-- Read access to source byte `k` (§12 ¶1). -/
def srcByte (k : Nat) : Access := ⟨96 + k, 1, 1, .read⟩

/-- Write access to destination byte `k` (§12 ¶1). -/
def dstByte (k : Nat) : Access := ⟨128 + k, 2, 1, .write⟩

/-- Representation supplied by the copy of byte `k`: the value and provenance of source byte
`k` (§16 ¶2). `cp_reads` shows that it is the abstract byte the copy read (§20.2 ¶1). -/
def copyRep (k : Nat) : Nat → UInt8 × Option Nat := fun _ => ptrRep k

/-- State after copying the first `k` bytes, one byte per write (§16 ¶2). -/
def cp : Nat → State
  | 0 => h13Src
  | k + 1 => (cp k).write (dstByte k) (copyRep k)

/-- Operations reaching `cp k`: set-up, then for each byte a read of the source byte and a
write of the destination byte (§15, §16). -/
def cpOps : Nat → List (Op Unit)
  | 0 => [.alloc 0 64 8 8 none, .alloc 0 96 8 8 none, .alloc 0 128 8 8 none,
      .write ⟨96, 1, 8, .write⟩ () ptrRep]
  | k + 1 => cpOps k ++ [.read (srcByte k) ()] ++ [.write (dstByte k) () (copyRep k)]

/-- Before copying byte `k`, the read of source byte `k` is `ok` and returns exactly the value
and provenance that `copyRep k` supplies (§15, §16 ¶5, §20.2 ¶1). -/
theorem cp_reads : ∀ k, k < 8 →
    read Witness.obR (srcByte k) () (cp k) trivial = .ok [.init (ptrRep k).1 (ptrRep k).2] := by
  decide

/-- Before copying byte `k`, the write of destination byte `k` satisfies the kernel write
conditions (§16.1–§16.3). -/
theorem cp_writes : ∀ k, k < 8 → CanWrite (cp k) (dstByte k) := by
  decide

/-- The copy of the first `k ≤ 8` bytes is an execution of `ok` steps from the empty state
(§20.3 ¶3). -/
theorem run_cp : ∀ k, k ≤ 8 → Run (cpOps k) (cp k)
  | 0, _ =>
    run_write (run_alloc (run_alloc (run_alloc (.nil _) (by decide)) (by decide)) (by decide))
      (by decide) trivial trivial
  | k + 1, hk =>
    run_write (run_read (run_cp k (Nat.le_of_succ_le hk)) (read_sound (cp_reads k hk)))
      (cp_writes k hk) trivial trivial

/-- The eight abstract bytes of `ptrRep`, each with provenance `0` (§10 ¶2). -/
def ptrBytes : List AByte :=
  [.init 64 (some 0), .init 0 (some 0), .init 0 (some 0), .init 0 (some 0),
    .init 0 (some 0), .init 0 (some 0), .init 0 (some 0), .init 0 (some 0)]

/-- H13a. Pointer bytes copied byte by byte, each write supplying the abstract byte just read.
Expected: the provenance of each byte is kept. Obtained, at relation level: every copy read is
`ok` with the byte's value and provenance, and after the copy the destination reads exactly
the source bytes, provenance `0` on each (§16 ¶2, §16 ¶5, §20.2 ¶1). Open obligation, not
declared passed: whether a byte copy of the language supplies the read provenance is not fixed
(§10 ¶4, §19 ¶3). Class N2. -/
theorem H13a : Run (cpOps 8) (cp 8) ∧
    (∀ k, k < 8 → ReadStep ctxR (srcByte k) () (cp k) (.ok [.init (ptrRep k).1 (ptrRep k).2])) ∧
    ReadStep ctxR ⟨128, 2, 8, .read⟩ () (cp 8) (.ok ptrBytes) ∧
    ReadStep ctxR ⟨96, 1, 8, .read⟩ () (cp 8) (.ok ptrBytes) :=
  ⟨run_cp 8 (Nat.le_refl _), fun k hk => read_sound (cp_reads k hk),
    readStep_of (by decide +kernel), readStep_of (by decide +kernel)⟩

/-- H13b. Rebuilding a usable access from the copied bytes or from the integer `64`.
Expected: to be arbitrated. Obtained: no verdict; the machine has no conversion from an integer
or from bytes to an access, and an access to address `64` gets `ok` or `ub` according to the
provenance a conversion rule would give it: `0` (the provenance stored in the copied bytes)
gives `ok`, `2` (the allocation holding the copied bytes) gives `ub`. Open obligation, not
declared passed (§19.2, §19.3, §19 ¶3). Class N2. -/
theorem H13b_open :
    WriteStep ctxW ⟨64, 0, 1, .write⟩ () w₁ (cp 8) (.ok ((cp 8).write ⟨64, 0, 1, .write⟩ w₁)) ∧
    WriteStep ctxW ⟨64, 2, 1, .write⟩ () w₁ (cp 8) .ub :=
  ⟨.ok ⟨by decide, trivial, trivial⟩, .ub fun h => absurd h.1 (by decide)⟩

/-! ## H14 — false static obligation -/

/-- Read obligations whose decidable part is `True` and whose static part is `P` at every read
(§20.3 ¶1, §20.3 ¶2): an explicit context with a false (`P = False`) or true (`P = True`)
static obligation. -/
def obStat (P : Prop) : ReadObl Unit :=
  { dec := fun _ _ _ => True, stat := fun _ _ _ => P, decInst := fun _ _ _ => instDecidableTrue }

/-- H14. Read of initialized bytes satisfying every kernel condition, under a context whose
static obligation is false. Expected: relation `ub`, interpreter not callable. Obtained: the
relation is `ub` (§20.1 ¶2, "including when the obligation is static"), and no proof of the
static part exists, so `read (obStat False) (rd 0) () a8w` cannot be applied (§20.3 ¶3).
Class N2. -/
theorem H14 :
    Exec (· = ·) (obStat False).toSpec ctxW [.alloc 0 96 8 8 (some 7), .write (wr 0) () Witness.w₀]
      State.empty a8w ∧
    CanRead a8w (rd 0) ∧ ReadStep (obStat False).toSpec (rd 0) () a8w .ub ∧
    ¬ (obStat False).stat a8w (rd 0) () :=
  ⟨run_write (run_alloc (.nil _) (by decide)) (by decide) trivial trivial, by decide,
    .ub fun h => h.2.2, id⟩

/-- H14 twin: same access, static obligation true. Expected `ok`; obtained `ok` by the
relation and by the interpreter, with the same bytes (§20.1 ¶2, §20.3 ¶3). Class N2. -/
theorem H14_twin :
    Exec (· = ·) (obStat True).toSpec ctxW [.alloc 0 96 8 8 (some 7), .write (wr 0) () Witness.w₀]
      State.empty a8w ∧
    ReadStep (obStat True).toSpec (rd 0) () a8w (.ok (writtenBytes Witness.w₀ 0 8)) ∧
    read (obStat True) (rd 0) () a8w trivial = .ok (writtenBytes Witness.w₀ 0 8) :=
  have hr : read (obStat True) (rd 0) () a8w trivial = .ok (writtenBytes Witness.w₀ 0 8) := by
    decide
  ⟨run_write (run_alloc (.nil _) (by decide)) (by decide) trivial trivial, read_sound hr, hr⟩

/-! ## H15, H16 — zero-size allocations, deallocation with a live access -/

/-- State of H15: two allocations of size `0` at base `96` in space `0` (§9 ¶3). -/
abbrev h15 : State := (State.empty.alloc 0 96 0 8 none).alloc 0 96 0 8 none

/-- H15. Two zero-size allocations live at the same base. Expected `ok`, distinct identities;
obtained: both creations `ok`, the state is admissible, identities `0` and `1` are both live
at base `96` with size `0` (§9 ¶3, §9 ¶8, §13 ¶1). Class N2. -/
theorem H15 : Run [.alloc 0 96 0 8 none, .alloc 0 96 0 8 none] h15 ∧ Admissible h15 ∧
    (∃ a, h15.allocs 0 = some a ∧ a.live = true ∧ a.base = 96 ∧ a.size = 0) ∧
    (∃ b, h15.allocs 1 = some b ∧ b.live = true ∧ b.base = 96 ∧ b.size = 0) :=
  have hr : Run [.alloc 0 96 0 8 none, .alloc 0 96 0 8 none] h15 :=
    run_alloc (run_alloc (.nil _) (by decide)) (by decide)
  ⟨hr, hr.admissible admissible_empty, ⟨_, rfl, rfl, rfl, rfl⟩, ⟨_, rfl, rfl, rfl, rfl⟩⟩

/-- State of H16: `a8w` (written through `wr 0`), then deallocation of `0` (§17 ¶3). -/
abbrev h16 : State := a8w.dealloc 0

/-- H16. Deallocation while the access `wr 0` designates the allocation, then use of that
access. Expected `ok`, then `ub`; obtained: the deallocation is `ok` (its conditions do not
mention existing accesses, §17.1, §17.2), then the write and the read through provenance `0`
are `ub` (§15.1, §16.1, §17 ¶3). Prevention belongs to the access discipline. Class N2. -/
theorem H16 :
    Run [.alloc 0 96 8 8 (some 7), .write (wr 0) () Witness.w₀, .dealloc 0 7] h16 ∧
    DeallocStep (· = ·) 0 7 a8w (.ok h16) ∧
    WriteStep ctxW (wr 0) () Witness.w₀ h16 .ub ∧ ReadStep ctxR (rd 0) () h16 .ub :=
  ⟨run_dealloc run_a8w (by decide), .ok (by decide), .ub fun h => absurd h.1 (by decide),
    readStep_of (by decide)⟩

/-! ## H17 — relation and interpreter -/

/-- On a state, every outcome of the read relation is the interpreter's result and conversely
(§20.3 ¶3, `read_sound`, `read_complete`). -/
theorem read_agree (ac : Access) (s : State) (o : ReadOutcome) :
    ReadStep ctxR ac () s o ↔ read Witness.obR ac () s trivial = o :=
  ⟨fun h => read_complete h trivial, read_sound⟩

/-- H17. Read by the relation and by the interpreter on admissible reached states. Expected:
same outcome, same value. Obtained: on `a8w` both give `ok` with the written bytes, on `a8`
both give `ub`, and the outcome sets coincide (§9 ¶8, §20.1, §20.2 ¶1, §20.3 ¶3). Class N2. -/
theorem H17 :
    Run [.alloc 0 96 8 8 (some 7), .write (wr 0) () Witness.w₀] a8w ∧ Admissible a8w ∧
    (∀ o, ReadStep ctxR (rd 0) () a8w o ↔ read Witness.obR (rd 0) () a8w trivial = o) ∧
    ReadStep ctxR (rd 0) () a8w (.ok (writtenBytes Witness.w₀ 0 8)) ∧
    read Witness.obR (rd 0) () a8w trivial = .ok (writtenBytes Witness.w₀ 0 8) ∧
    Run [.alloc 0 96 8 8 (some 7)] a8 ∧ Admissible a8 ∧
    (∀ o, ReadStep ctxR (rd 0) () a8 o ↔ read Witness.obR (rd 0) () a8 trivial = o) ∧
    ReadStep ctxR (rd 0) () a8 .ub ∧ read Witness.obR (rd 0) () a8 trivial = .ub :=
  ⟨run_a8w, run_a8w.admissible admissible_empty, read_agree _ _, H04_twin.2, by decide,
    run_a8, run_a8.admissible admissible_empty, read_agree _ _, H04.2, by decide⟩

end Ern.Corpus.MM2H

# ERN — Jalon 3 : matériel pour revue unique

**Objet :** validation adversariale du Memory Model (spec 1) après les jalons 1 et 2.
**Contenu :** les trois corpus mis à jour, le contrat du pool de handles, le cadrage de la décision `NoLock`, le registre des obligations inter-spécifications.
**Statut :** matériel de conception, non normatif. Version 2 : corrections de la revue unique de GPT intégrées (contrat du pool, corpus, calendrier, scénarios Weld).

## 0. Règles du jalon 3

1. **Oracle indépendant.** Le verdict attendu d'un cas vient de sa source (clause de MM-02 v0.4, de MM-03.3 v0.3, arbitrage, ou usage déclaré), jamais du comportement des modules. Un cas sans source qui tranche est marqué « à arbitrer ».
2. **Jumeau positif.** Chaque rejet a un jumeau minimal accepté : même séquence sans l'élément fautif. Un rejet qui persiste dans le jumeau est un défaut de construction.
3. **États atteints.** Chaque cas est construit depuis l'état initial par des pas autorisés.
4. **Pas de correction silencieuse.** Un verdict obtenu différent de l'attendu est rapporté avec l'état et le pas en cause.
5. **Classement.** Chaque cas relève de : noyau MM-03 (`N3`), machine MM-02 (`N2`), raffinement (`R`), instance de bibliothèque (`Lib` : arène, pool), ou d'une autre spécification (spec 2, 3, 4, 11). Les cas d'une autre spécification restent des obligations inter-spécifications ; ils ne bloquent pas la clôture du jalon 3.
6. **Couverture.** La colonne « Couvert » indique un témoin déjà produit pendant les jalons 1 et 2, quand il est identifié avec certitude. Le jalon 3 rejoue tous les cas depuis l'état initial, couverts ou non, dans un module de cas séparé.
7. **Cible des corpus.** MM3-H et MM23-H sont encodés au jalon 3 sur les brouillons, sans modifier `MM02`, `MM03` ni `MM23`. MM2-H : ses verdicts sont révisés au jalon 3, mais sa validation exécutable reste une obligation de la reconstruction de référence ; le jalon 3 ne le déclare pas validé.
8. **Écarts connus.** Un cas dont le verdict attendu repose sur une décision non encore appliquée au brouillon (MM23-H15, H16) est encodé avec le verdict obtenu, marqué « écart connu », et inscrit au registre de reconstruction. Il n'est jamais présenté comme réussi.

---

### G. Handles (instance `HandlePool`, §4)

## 3. Corpus MM23-H — raffinement

La plupart des obligations sont déjà établies par le jalon 2 ; le jalon 3 rejoue chaque cas comme exécution traduite par `simulation`.

| H02 | `reset` d'arène, puis accès par une ancienne autorité de bloc | aucun programme sûr n'y parvient ; MM-02 l'accepterait (allocation vivante) | à énoncer (R4 + `ResetPre`) |

import Ern.Corpus.Runner

/-!
# Corpus MM3-H: access discipline, sections A–F, H, I (test module)

The cases of corpus MM3-H of the Jalon 3 material (`ERN_Jalon3_materiel.md`, §1; non-normative
design material), run on the reference kernel and arena of
`specs/ERN_Memory_Model_Specification_v0.md` (§60–§78), plus new cases fixed by spec clauses and the
usage scenario W3 (material §5b). This is a test module: no model module imports it.

Each case is a run from `LState.init statics` (§47) by the runner (`Ern.Corpus.Runner`):
`RunsTo k statics os L` states that every step is `ok` and that `L` is library-reachable and its
kernel state `Reachable` (§57). The verdict of the step under test is stated with the relation of
its operation (`DeriveStep`, `TransferStep`, `IssueD`, `ResetD`, …) on the reached state and
decided by `decide`. Each docstring gives the expected verdict from the case's source (the
material, or the spec clause for new cases), the obtained verdict, the class (material §0, rule 5:
`N3` kernel, `Lib` library instance, `spec 3` another specification) and the positive twin (rule 2:
the same sequence without the faulty element, accepted). A case whose obtained verdict differs from
the expected one is kept with its expected verdict and marked **MISMATCH** with its cause; no case
is corrected.

Twins that are not literally the same sequence without one faulty step:
* another destination, target, parameter or identity in place of the faulty one: H04 (the other
  element), H13 (`z`), H18 (the local leaf 3), H21 (a `Modify` parameter), H25 (a `Modify`
  parameter on the static), H29 (a `Modify` parameter), H50 `transfer` (the stored authority on
  the local 4), H50 `issue` (the value 2), H51 direct form (the view on `u`), S63_8 (the stored
  authority on the local 6), S56 (`internal` 5), S77_2 (the destination 3 outside the region,
  `fail`; the available region `[6]`, `ok`);
* further steps that lift the blocking before the step under test: H11 (`endUse` of `v2` and of
  the leaf 6), H17 (`endUse` of the block value, then `free` of the storage 4 instead of the leaf
  5), H19 (`endUse` of the child value), H26 second twin (the contract with `ExternalDone`, then
  `unpin`), H27b (three `release`), W3 (`endUse` of the structure and of the block values);
* a pairing given by the material: H05 (its own twin), H21b (H37);
* a faulty element of several steps, removed: H03, S77_6 (`derive` and `store`), H51 through a
  helper (the view, or its `store`), H49 (the six steps of the cycle: removing only its stores
  leaves the `reject`, for another cause);
* no twin: the `reset` `reject` in the state `h49` of H49, which persists without the cycle
  (construction defect by rule 2, recorded there); the reception `transfer` `reject` of H16, a
  **MISMATCH** whose expected verdict is `ok`.

Local shapes are lists of (parent, kind) (§72, §71.1); `lf` is a root leaf, `pt p` a part of `p`.
Place and authority identities are list indices (§38): `enterFrame` appends the locals and one
root authority per root local; `alloc` appends the shape and one root authority; `derive` and
`split` append the derived authorities; `issue` appends one block authority; `reset` appends one
(released) authority.

Not encoded here:
* section G (H30–H34b, H44, handle pools) and the usage scenarios W1, W2 (they use a handle pool):
  later wave (`HandlePool`);
* the cross-registry cases of §56 (a pool and an arena, or two pools, on one `internal`): later
  wave; only the arena registry exists here (`S56`);
* section J, out of the kernel, classified by the material: H38 get-or-insert cache (spec 3,
  flow-sensitive liveness, §25, §32); H39 suspended coroutine holding a `Modify` parameter
  (specs 2 and 3, §29, §81); H40 raw pointer used during a call (spec 3 and the boundary of §19,
  §81); H41 concurrent `writeShared` (spec 2, §18, §24, §68); H42 `defer free(x)` then
  `transfer(x)` (spec 3, `defer` is outside the kernel, §73, §81); H43 resource with a release
  obligation (resource specification, §7).
-/

namespace Ern.Corpus.MM3H

open Ern.MemoryModel.Access Ern.MemoryModel.Arena Ern.Corpus

/-! ## Test contracts and shapes (§48, §72) -/

/-- The empty test contract (§48): nothing shared, pinned, externally done or deallocable. -/
abbrev K0 : K := KD.toK {}

/-- A root leaf of a local shape (§72, §71.1). -/
abbrev lf : Option Nat × Nat := (none, 0)

/-- A leaf part of the shape element `p` (§72, §71.1). -/
abbrev pt (p : Nat) : Option Nat × Nat := (some p, 0)

/-- A structure 0 with the parts 1 and 2 (§40, §72). -/
def S2 : LocalShape := [lf, pt 0, pt 0]

/-- A write of `ls` rejected for every authority of the state is rejected for every authority
(§67.1: the writing authority is exercisable, hence exists, §43). -/
theorem write_rejected {s : S3} {ls : List Nat}
    (h : ∀ a ∈ List.range s.A.length, ¬ Write3Pre s a ls) (a : Nat) :
    Write3Step a ls s .reject :=
  .reject fun hp => h a (List.mem_range.2 (exercisable_lt hp.exercisable)) hp

/-- A read of `ls` rejected for every authority of the state is rejected for every authority
(§66.2: the reading authority is exercisable, hence exists, §43). -/
theorem read_rejected {s : S3} {ls : List Nat}
    (h : ∀ a ∈ List.range s.A.length, ¬ Read3Pre s a ls) (a : Nat) :
    Read3Step a ls s .reject :=
  .reject fun hp => h a (List.mem_range.2 (exercisable_lt hp.exercisable)) hp

/-- The preconditions of `transfer` other than local self-blocking prevention (§63.1–§63.7), the
fields of `TransferPre` but `noSelfLock`: used to show that §63.8 alone rejects a transfer. -/
def TransferPreBut638 (k : K) (s : S3) (src dst : Nat) : Prop :=
  s.Usable src ∧ s.Usable dst ∧ HasRight s .modify src ∧ HasRight s .modify dst ∧
    SameShape s.P src dst ∧ (∀ l ∈ footprint s.P src, s.I l = .init) ∧
    (∀ l ∈ footprint s.P dst, s.I l ≠ .init) ∧ ¬ overlap s.P src dst ∧
    (∀ j ∈ List.range s.A.length, ¬ ActiveDerivedOutside s src j) ∧
    (∀ l ∈ footprint s.P src, ¬ k.Pinned l ∧ s.pin l = false) ∧
    (∀ x ∈ movedDeps s src, s.Active x) ∧ AnchorOrder (transferEff s src dst) ∧
    (∀ x ∈ List.range s.A.length, AnchorMoves s src x →
      ∀ q ∈ List.range s.P.length, (transferEff s src dst).Usable q →
        OptP ((transferEff s src dst).A[x]?) (fun y => y.active = true → y.holder = .place q →
          EffAnchorOK (transferEff s src dst) x ((transferEff s src dst).pframe q)) True)

/-- Decidability of `TransferPreBut638` (§63). -/
instance (k : K) [DecidablePred k.Pinned] (s : S3) (src dst : Nat) :
    Decidable (TransferPreBut638 k s src dst) := by
  unfold TransferPreBut638; infer_instance

/-- The static preconditions of `issue` other than local self-blocking prevention (§77.1, §77.2),
the fields of `IssueStatic` but `dstNotIn`: used to show that this clause alone rejects. -/
def IssueStaticBut (s : S3) (E : ArenaEntry) (region : List Nat) (dst : Nat) : Prop :=
  s.Active E.internal ∧ MetaRight s E ∧ (∀ l ∈ region, l ∈ footprint s.P E.storage) ∧
    s.Usable dst ∧ isLeaf s.P dst ∧
    (∀ j ∈ List.range s.A.length,
      OptP (s.A[j]?) (fun z => z.active = true → z.holder ≠ .place dst) True) ∧
    HasRight s .modify dst

/-- Decidability of `IssueStaticBut` (§77). -/
instance (s : S3) (E : ArenaEntry) (region : List Nat) (dst : Nat) :
    Decidable (IssueStaticBut s E region dst) := by
  unfold IssueStaticBut; infer_instance

/-! ## A. Exclusivity and indirect aliasing -/

/-- Run of H01 (§72, §60): frame 1 with structure 0 (parts 1, 2, root authority 0);
`derive(0, [1, 2], Modify)` gives the first parameter, authority 1. -/
def h01o : List Op := [.enter [] S2, .derive 0 [1, 2] .modify]
/-- State reached by `h01o` (§57). -/
def h01 : LState := final K0 [] h01o

/-- **H01** (material §1 A, class N3). Two parameters derived from one local, `Modify` on the
whole, then `Observe` on a part. Expected (material): `reject`. Obtained: `reject`: the root has no
effective mode on the part, covered by the active `Modify` descendant 1 (§43 case 3), so the
`Observe` derivation exceeds it (§60.2). Twin without the first parameter: the `derive` is `ok`;
and the call with the first parameter alone is `ok` (§72). -/
theorem H01 : RunsTo K0 [] h01o h01 ∧ DeriveStep 0 [1] .observe h01.kern .reject ∧
    Runs K0 [] [.enter [] S2, .derive 0 [1] .observe] ∧ Runs K0 [] (h01o ++ [.enter [1] []]) :=
  ⟨runsTo (by decide), .reject (by decide), runsTo (by decide), runsTo (by decide)⟩

/-- State reached by `h04o` (§57). -/

/-- **H04** (material §1 A, class N3). Swap of two elements: by `split` then two writes, `ok`; by
two `derive Modify` of the same element, the second `reject`. Expected (material): `ok` /
`reject`. Obtained: `ok` (§61, §67) / `reject` (§43 case 3, §60.2, §85: a second derivation over
the same leaf is not legal merely by having a distinct name). Twin of the rejection: `derive
Modify` of the other element, `ok`.
STMT: : Runs K0 [] [.enter [] S2, .split 0 [[1], [2]], .write 1 [1], .write 2 [2]] ∧
    RunsTo K0 [] h04o h04 ∧ DeriveStep 0 [1] .modify h04.kern .reject ∧
    Runs K0 [] (h04o ++ [.derive 0 [2] .modify])
===== H05
Run of H05 (§72, §67): structure `x` (0, fields `f` = 1 and 2) and `tmp` (leaf 3); `x`
written. -/
def h05o : List Op := [.enter [] (S2 ++ [lf]), .write 0 [1, 2]]
/-- State reached by `h05o` (§57). -/
def h05 : LState := final K0 [] h05o

/-- **H05** (material §1 A, class N3). `transfer(x, x.f)`; twin `transfer(x.f, tmp)` then
`transfer(tmp, x.f)`, the destination `Moved` and of the same shape. Expected (material):
`reject` / `ok`. Obtained: `reject` (§63.2 shapes differ; §63.3 the destination is `Init` and the
footprints overlap) / `ok`.
STMT: : RunsTo K0 [] h05o h05 ∧ TransferStep K0 0 1 h05.kern .reject ∧
    Runs K0 [] (h05o ++ [.transfer 1 3, .transfer 3 1])
===== H11
Run of H11 (§71, §76, §77, §63): frame 1 with arena value 0, allocator 1, values `v1` (2) and
`v2` (3); storage 4 (leaves 5, 6) owned by 0, `internal` its root authority 4; blocks 5 on `[5]`
to `v1` and 6 on `[6]` to `v2`; `v1` transferred into the leaf 6 of the block of `v2`. -/
def h11o : List Op := [.enter [] [lf, lf, lf, lf], .write 1 [1], .alloc 1 0 [lf, pt 4, pt 4],
  .write 0 [0], .newArena 4 4, .issue 0 [5] 2, .issue 0 [6] 3, .transfer 2 6]
/-- State reached by `h11o` (§57). -/
def h11 : LState := final K0 [] h11o

/-- **H11** (material §1 B, class Lib). An arena buffer stored into another block of the same
arena. Expected (material): `transfer` `ok`; `reset` `reject` while one lives. Obtained: the
`transfer` is `ok` (§63; §63.8 holds: block 5 covers 5, not the new holder 6); `reset` is `reject`
(§78.2: block 5 is active and covers leaf 5; `derive` of `internal` over the storage exceeds its
effective right, Part XIV). Twin: after `endUse` of `v2` and of the leaf 6, `reset` is `ok`.
STMT: : RunsTo K0 [] h11o h11 ∧ ResetD 0 h11 .reject ∧
    Runs K0 [] (h11o ++ [.endUse 3, .endUse 6, .reset 0])
===== H13
Run of H13 (§72, §71): frame 1 with allocator 0, `x` (1) and `z` (2), `x` written; `y` (3)
allocated, owned by `x`, its root authority 3 held by `x`. -/
def h13o : List Op := [.enter [] [lf, lf, lf], .write 0 [0], .write 1 [1], .alloc 0 1 [lf]]
/-- State reached by `h13o` (§57). -/
def h13 : LState := final K0 [] h13o

/-- **H13** (material §1 C, class N3). Ownership cycle: `x` owns `y`, then `y` receives `x` by
transfer. Expected (material): `reject`. Obtained: `reject` by §63.8 alone (§63.1–§63.7 hold):
the root authority 3 of `y`, held by `x`, would be held by `corr(x) = y` and covers the leaf `y`
(§40, §88). Twin: the transfer of `x` into `z` is `ok`.
STMT: : RunsTo K0 [] h13o h13 ∧ TransferStep K0 1 3 h13.kern .reject ∧
    TransferPreBut638 K0 h13.kern 1 3 ∧ ¬ NoLocalSelfLock h13.kern 1 3 ∧
    Runs K0 [] (h13o ++ [.transfer 1 2])
===== H16
Test contract of H16 (§70.2, §80): place 3 deallocable by the authority 7. -/
abbrev KF3 : K := KD.toK { dealloc := [3], compat := [(3, 7)] }

/-- Prefix of H16 (§72, §71, §60): frame 1 with allocator 0, `x` (1) and the result `R` (2);
storage 3 owned by `x`, written; parameters 4 (`Modify` on `x`) and 5 (`Modify` on `R`) passed to
frame 2, which has the local 4. -/
def h16p : List Op := [.enter [] [lf, lf, lf], .write 0 [0], .write 1 [1], .alloc 0 1 [lf],
  .write 3 [3], .derive 1 [1] .modify, .derive 2 [2] .modify, .enter [4, 5] [lf]]
/-- State reached by `h16p` (§57). -/
def h16a : LState := final KF3 [] h16p
/-- Run of H16 as the kernel can run it (§70, §73): the callee frees the storage through its
parameter on `x`, then returns. -/
def h16o : List Op := h16p ++ [.free 3 7, .exit]
/-- State reached by `h16o` (§57). -/
def h16 : LState := final KF3 [] h16o

/-- **H16** (material §1 C, class N3). The callee receives by transfer a value owning a storage,
frees it, returns the value; the caller reads that storage. Expected (material): `ok`, then
`reject`. Obtained: the reception, `transfer` of `x` into the callee's local, is `reject`: the
parameter 4 is an active derived authority covering `x` held outside it (§63.4, §45). With the
storage freed through the parameter on `x` (`ok`) and the return (`ok`), the caller's read of the
storage is `reject` for every authority (§66.1: the leaf belongs to no usable place, §70 effect).
Twin without the `free`: the read is `ok`. **MISMATCH** on the reception (expected `ok`, obtained
`reject`); cause: case defect, the reception by value is a calling convention deferred to Spec 3
(§45, §81) and the literal kernel `transfer` is rejected by §63.4.
STMT: : RunsTo KF3 [] h16p h16a ∧ TransferStep KF3 1 4 h16a.kern .reject ∧
    ActiveDerivedOutside h16a.kern 1 4 ∧ RunsTo KF3 [] h16o h16 ∧
    (∀ a, Read3Step a [3] h16.kern .reject) ∧ Runs KF3 [] (h16p ++ [.exit, .read 3 [3]])
===== H19
Run of H19 (§76, §77): storage 4 (leaf 5) owned by the arena value 0; parent arena on 4; block
5 on `[5]` issued to 2; child arena on the leaf 5 with `internal` the block 5, its arena value 2. -/
def h19o : List Op := [.enter [] [lf, lf, lf, lf], .write 1 [1], .alloc 1 0 [lf, pt 4],
  .write 0 [0], .newArena 4 4, .issue 0 [5] 2, .newArena 5 5]
/-- State reached by `h19o` (§57). -/
def h19 : LState := final K0 [] h19o

/-- **H19** (material §1 D, class Lib). Nested arena: `reset` of the parent while the child
lives, then after `endUse` of the child value. Expected (material): `reject`, then `ok`. Obtained:
`reject` (§78.2: the child's `internal`, block 5, is active and covers leaf 5), then `ok` (§69
effect releases it; §78).
STMT: : RunsTo K0 [] h19o h19 ∧ ResetD 0 h19 .reject ∧
    Runs K0 [] (h19o ++ [.endUse 2, .reset 0])
===== H21
Test contract of H21 (§68.1, §80): the arena value 0 is `SharedMutable`. -/
abbrev KA : K := KD.toK { shared := [0] }

/-- Prefix of H21 (§71, §76): frame 1 with arena value 0, allocator 1, buffer 2; storage 3
(leaves 4, 5) owned by 0; arena on 3 with `internal` 3. -/
def h21p : List Op := [.enter [] [lf, lf, lf], .write 1 [1], .alloc 1 0 [lf, pt 3, pt 3],
  .write 0 [0], .newArena 3 3]
/-- Run of H21 (§60, §72, §68): the caller passes 4, `Observe` on the arena value, and 5,
`Modify` on its buffer; the callee (local 6) updates the arena metadata by `writeShared`. -/
def h21o : List Op := h21p ++ [.derive 0 [0] .observe, .derive 2 [2] .modify, .enter [4, 5] [lf],
  .writeShared 4 [0]]
/-- State reached by `h21o` (§57). -/
def h21 : LState := final KA [] h21o

/-- **H21** (material §1 D, class Lib). A callee that only observes the arena issues a block to a
local, then returns the block. Expected (material): `ok`. Obtained: the `writeShared` on the
metadata is `ok` (§68), but the `issue` is `reject`: `MetaRight` requires exercisable `Modify` on
the arena value and `writeShared` alone does not satisfy it (§36, §77.1). Twin, the same run with a
`Modify` parameter on the arena value: `issue`, `transfer` of the block value to the caller and
`exitFrame` are `ok`. **MISMATCH** (expected `ok`, obtained `reject`); cause: spec change (§36,
§77.1).
STMT: : RunsTo KA [] h21o h21 ∧ IssueD KA 0 [4] 6 h21 .reject ∧
    OptP (h21.arenas[0]?) (fun E => ¬ MetaRight h21.kern E) False ∧
    Runs KA [] (h21p ++ [.derive 0 [0] .modify, .derive 2 [2] .modify, .enter [4, 5] [lf],
      .writeShared 4 [0], .issue 0 [4] 6, .transfer 6 2, .exit])
===== H22
Run of H22 (§72, §74): frame 1 with `x` (0), written and pinned, and `y` (1). -/
def h22o : List Op := [.enter [] [lf, lf], .write 0 [0], .pin 0]
/-- State reached by `h22o` (§57). -/
def h22 : LState := final K0 [] h22o

/-- **H22** (material §1 E, class N3). Transfer of a value whose in-place leaf is pinned / of a
value whose owned storage only is pinned. Expected (material): `reject` / `ok`. Obtained:
`reject` (§63.5) / `ok` (§63.5: owned storage not moved does not prevent the transfer; §87). Twin
of the rejection, without the pin: `ok`.
STMT: : RunsTo K0 [] h22o h22 ∧ TransferStep K0 0 1 h22.kern .reject ∧
    Runs K0 [] [.enter [] [lf, lf], .write 0 [0], .transfer 0 1] ∧
    Runs K0 [] [.enter [] [lf, lf, lf], .write 0 [0], .write 1 [1], .alloc 0 1 [lf], .pin 3,
      .transfer 1 2]
===== H24
Statics of H24 (§47): the MMIO leaf 0, `Init`, and the leaf 1, `Uninit`. -/
def stM : Statics := [((none, none, 0), true), ((none, none, 0), false)]
/-- Test contract of H24 (§74, §75, §80): the static leaf 0 is `K.Pinned`. -/
abbrev KM : K := KD.toK { pinned := [0] }

/-- **H24** (material §1 E, class N3). A static MMIO region pinned by `K.Pinned`, directly owned
by the base frame (`StaticPinnedBottom`, §75): `transfer` and `endUse`. Expected (material):
`reject`, `reject`. Obtained: `reject` (§63.5), `reject` (§69.4). Twin, the same static not
pinned: both `ok`.
STMT: : Runs KM stM [] ∧ StaticPinnedBottom KM stM ∧
    TransferStep KM 0 1 (S3.init stM) .reject ∧ EndUseStep KM 0 (S3.init stM) .reject ∧
    Runs K0 stM [.transfer 0 1] ∧ Runs K0 stM [.endUse 0]
===== H26
Test contract of H26 (§70.2, §80): place 2 deallocable by the authority 7. -/
abbrev KP : K := KD.toK { dealloc := [2], compat := [(2, 7)] }
/-- Test contract of the twin of H26 (§75, §80): the same, with `ExternalDone` on 2. -/
abbrev KPd : K := KD.toK { done := [2], dealloc := [2], compat := [(2, 7)] }
/-- Run of H26 (§74): the allocated storage 2 pinned. -/
def h26o : List Op := h14p ++ [.pin 2]
/-- State reached by `h26o` (§57). -/
def h26 : LState := final KP [] h26o

/-- **H26** (material §1 E, class N3). `free` of a pinned storage; `unpin` without `ExternalDone`.
Expected (material): `reject`, `reject`. Obtained: `reject` (§70.4), `reject` (§75). Twins:
`free` without the pin, `ok`; with `ExternalDone`, `unpin` then `free`, `ok`.
STMT: : RunsTo KP [] h26o h26 ∧ FreeStep KP 2 7 h26.kern .reject ∧
    UnpinStep KP 2 h26.kern .reject ∧ Runs KP [] (h14p ++ [.free 2 7]) ∧
    Runs KPd [] (h14p ++ [.pin 2, .unpin 2, .free 2 7])
===== H27b
Prefix of H27b (§72, §71, §60, §65): frame 1 with structure `a` (0, parts 1, 2), structure `b`
(3, parts 4, 5) and allocator 6; storage 7 allocated, owned by `a`, its root authority 3 held by
`a`; 4, `Modify` on 7 from that root; 5, `Modify` on `a`; 6 and 7, `Modify` on 1 and 2 from 5,
stored into 4 and 5; 8, `Modify` on `b`; the call passes 4, 5 and 8. -/
def h27bp : List Op := [.enter [] [lf, pt 0, pt 0, lf, pt 3, pt 3, lf], .write 2 [6],
  .alloc 6 0 [lf], .derive 3 [7] .modify, .derive 0 [1, 2] .modify, .derive 5 [1] .modify,
  .derive 5 [2] .modify, .derive 1 [4, 5] .modify, .store 6 4, .store 7 5, .enter [4, 5, 8] []]
/-- State reached by `h27bp` (§57). -/
def h27b : LState := final K0 [] h27bp

/-- **H27b** (material §1 F, class spec 3). The same attempt after releasing the authorities that
blocked the origin: the callee releases its parameter 4 on the owned storage 7, then the
authorities 6 and 7 that kept its parameter 5 from exercising the root of `a`; the write of 7
through that storage's root 3 is then accepted. Expected (material): `ok` in the kernel, strong
protection deferred to Spec 3. Obtained: at entry the write is `reject` (§72.3); after the
releases, `ok` (§72 last paragraph: entry protection only, the rest deferred to Spec 3). The
storage is allocated (§71) and owned by `a`, since locals are owned directly by their frame (§39,
§72).
STMT: : RunsTo K0 [] h27bp h27b ∧ Write3Step 3 [7] h27b.kern .reject ∧
    Runs K0 [] (h27bp ++ [.release 4, .release 6, .release 7, .write 3 [7]])
===== H49
Run of H49 (§60, §65, §62): the cycle of H48 closed through the helper 9, `Modify` on 6 from
7, then the helper released. -/
def h49o : List Op := h48o ++ [.derive 7 [6] .modify, .store 8 6, .release 9]
/-- State reached by `h49o` (§57). -/
def h49 : LState := final K0 [] h49o
/-- State reached by `h49o` and the `endUse` of the block values 2 and 3, which ends the blocks 5
and 6 (§69 effect, §57). -/
def h49e : LState := final K0 [] (h49o ++ [.endUse 2, .endUse 3])

/-- **H49** (material §1 I, class N3). The same cycle, closed through a helper authority, then
`release` of the helper. Expected (material): to arbitrate. Obtained: `ok`, with a residual
blocking (material §5: held authorities that nobody can exercise block a `reset`): the authorities
7 and 8 are exercisable in no mode; after the `endUse` of the block values 2 and 3 they stay so,
active, held by the leaves 5 and 6, derived from `internal` through the blocks and covering the
leaves 6 and 5, and `reset` is `reject` (§78.2; §65 last paragraph and §27: `NoLock` is not
adopted; §88: indirect blocking compatible with safety may remain). Twin of that `reject`: the
same sequence without the cycle (the six steps after `fao`), `ok`. Dropping only one or both
`store` steps does not lift it: an authority left with the frame still covers its leaf (§78.2, a
different, releasable cause). The `reset` `reject` in `h49` itself persists in that twin (on
`fao` the blocks 5 and 6 are still held by the values 2 and 3, §78.2): by rule 2 it is a
construction defect, kept as a fact and not as the residual blocking of the case. **MISMATCH** in form (expected "to arbitrate", obtained `ok`);
cause: spec change, spec v0 now determines the verdict (§65, §88).
STMT: : RunsTo K0 [] h49o h49 ∧ ¬ h49.kern.ExercisableAt 7 .observe ∧
    ¬ h49.kern.ExercisableAt 8 .observe ∧ ResetD 0 h49 .reject ∧
    RunsTo K0 [] (h49o ++ [.endUse 2, .endUse 3]) h49e ∧ ¬ h49e.kern.ExercisableAt 7 .observe ∧
    ¬ h49e.kern.ExercisableAt 8 .observe ∧ ResetD 0 h49e .reject ∧
    Runs K0 [] (fao ++ [.endUse 2, .endUse 3, .reset 0])
===== H50_transfer
Run of H50, `transfer` part (§72, §60, §65): structure 0 (field 1), structure 2 (field 3),
local 4; 3, `Modify` on the field 3, stored into the field 1. -/
def h50to : List Op := [.enter [] [lf, pt 0, lf, pt 2, lf], .derive 1 [3] .modify, .store 3 1]
/-- State reached by `h50to` (§57). -/
def h50t : LState := final K0 [] h50to

/-- **H50**, `transfer` part (material §1 I, class N3). An authority transferred into the place
it covers: structure 0 is transferred into structure 2 while its field 1 holds 3, which covers
the field 3 = `corr(1)`. Expected (material): to arbitrate. Obtained: `reject` by §63.8 alone
(local self-blocking prevention; §63.1–§63.7 hold; §88). Twin, the stored authority covering the
local 4 instead: `ok`. **MISMATCH** (expected "to arbitrate", obtained `reject`); cause: spec
change (§63.8).
STMT: : RunsTo K0 [] h50to h50t ∧ TransferStep K0 0 2 h50t.kern .reject ∧
    TransferPreBut638 K0 h50t.kern 0 2 ∧ ¬ NoLocalSelfLock h50t.kern 0 2 ∧
    Runs K0 [] [.enter [] [lf, pt 0, lf, pt 2, lf], .derive 2 [4] .modify, .store 3 1,
      .transfer 0 2]
===== H50_issue
State after the first five steps of `fao`, the arena created and nothing issued (§57). -/
def h50i : LState := final K0 [] (fao.take 5)

/-- **H50**, `issue` part (material §1 I, class Lib). A block issued into a leaf of its own region
(`issue(0, [5], 5)`, the region available). Expected (material): to arbitrate. Obtained: `reject`,
static, by local self-blocking prevention alone: the other static preconditions hold and the
destination is in the region (§77.2, §88). Twin, the same issue into the value 2: `ok`.
**MISMATCH** (expected "to arbitrate", obtained `reject`); cause: spec change (§77.2).
STMT: : RunsTo K0 [] (fao.take 5) h50i ∧ IssueD K0 0 [5] 5 h50i .reject ∧
    OptP (h50i.arenas[0]?) (fun E => IssueStaticBut h50i.kern E [5] 5 ∧
      ¬ IssueStatic h50i.kern E [5] 5) False ∧
    Runs K0 [] (fao.take 5 ++ [.issue 0 [5] 2])
===== H51
Prefix of H51 (§72, §71): frame 1 with allocator 0, `v` (1) and `u` (2), written; storage 3
(element 4) owned by `v`, its root authority 3 held by `v`. -/
def h51p : List Op := [.enter [] [lf, lf, lf], .write 0 [0], .write 1 [1], .write 2 [2],
  .alloc 0 1 [lf, pt 3]]
/-- Run of H51, direct form (§60): 4, `Observe` on `v`. -/
def h51no : List Op := h51p ++ [.derive 1 [1] .observe]
/-- State reached by `h51no` (§57). -/
def h51n : LState := final K0 [] h51no
/-- Run of H51 through a helper (§60, §65, §62): 4, `Modify` on the element, held by the frame;
5, `Observe` on `v`, stored into the element; the helper released. -/
def h51o : List Op := h51p ++ [.derive 3 [4] .modify, .derive 1 [1] .observe, .store 5 4,
  .release 4]
/-- State reached by `h51o` (§57). -/
def h51 : LState := final K0 [] h51o

/-- **H51** (material §1 I, class N3). An element of a storage owned by `v` holds a view on `v`.
Expected (material): to arbitrate. Obtained: the direct `store` is `reject`: the view takes away
the frame's `Modify` on `v`, hence on the storage it owns (§43 case 4, §65.2, §65.5); twin with
the view on another value `u`: `ok`. Through a helper on the element, then its `release`, the
configuration is reached (`ok`); then `v` can be neither written, nor relieved of the view, nor
ended (`reject`, §67.1, §62.2, §69.1), while the view stays exercisable in `Observe`; the exit of
the frame is `ok` (§88: residual blocking). Twins of these three rejections: the same sequence
without the view on `v` (its `derive` and its `store`), then the write of `v` through its root,
`ok`, or its `endUse`, `ok`; the same sequence without the `store` of the view, then its
`release`, `ok`. With only the `store` dropped, the write and the `endUse` stay `reject` for a
different cause: the view, then held by the frame, is active on `v` (§43 case 4, §67.1, §69.2)
and releasable. **MISMATCH** in form (expected "to arbitrate", obtained `reject` / `ok`); cause:
spec change, spec v0 now determines the verdicts (§65.2, §88).
STMT: : RunsTo K0 [] h51no h51n ∧ StoreStep 4 4 h51n.kern .reject ∧
    Runs K0 [] (h51p ++ [.derive 2 [2] .observe, .store 4 4]) ∧
    RunsTo K0 [] h51o h51 ∧ (∀ a, Write3Step a [1] h51.kern .reject) ∧
    ReleaseStep 5 h51.kern .reject ∧ EndUseStep K0 1 h51.kern .reject ∧
    h51.kern.ExercisableAt 5 .observe ∧ Runs K0 [] (h51o ++ [.exit]) ∧
    Runs K0 [] (h51p ++ [.derive 3 [4] .modify, .release 4, .write 1 [1]]) ∧
    Runs K0 [] (h51p ++ [.derive 3 [4] .modify, .derive 1 [1] .observe, .release 4, .release 5]) ∧
    Runs K0 [] (h51p ++ [.derive 3 [4] .modify, .release 4, .endUse 1])
===== S77_2
State after the first six steps of `fao`: block 5 on `[5]` issued to 2, so the leaf 5 is not
available (§46, §77). -/
def s772 : LState := final K0 [] (fao.take 6)

/-- **S77.2** (new case, §77.2; class Lib). Issue into a leaf of the region when the region is
unavailable. Expected (§77.2: the condition is static and checked before an availability `fail`):
`reject`. Obtained: `reject` (`issue(0, [5], 5)`: the other static preconditions hold, the
destination is in the region and the region is unavailable). Twin without the faulty element,
the destination 3 outside the region: `fail` (§77.4), as prescribed for an unavailable region;
with an available region (`issue(0, [6], 3)`): `ok`.
STMT: : RunsTo K0 [] (fao.take 6) s772 ∧ IssueD K0 0 [5] 5 s772 .reject ∧
    OptP (s772.arenas[0]?) (fun E => IssueStaticBut s772.kern E [5] 5 ∧
      ¬ IssueStatic s772.kern E [5] 5 ∧ ¬ Avail E [5]) False ∧
    IssueD K0 0 [5] 3 s772 .fail ∧ Runs K0 [] fao
===== W3
Run of W3, literal reading (§71, §76, §77, §60, §65): frame 1 with arena value 0, allocator
1, block values 2, 3, 4 and structure 5 (fields 6, 7, 8); storage 9 (leaves 10, 11, 12) owned by
0, `internal` 6; three blocks issued to 2, 3, 4; three views (10, 11, 12), `Observe` on the
blocks, stored into the fields. -/
def w3o : List Op := [.enter [] [lf, lf, lf, lf, lf, lf, pt 5, pt 5, pt 5], .write 1 [1],
  .alloc 1 0 [lf, pt 9, pt 9, pt 9], .write 0 [0], .newArena 9 6, .issue 0 [10] 2,
  .issue 0 [11] 3, .issue 0 [12] 4, .derive 7 [10] .observe, .derive 8 [11] .observe,
  .derive 9 [12] .observe, .store 10 6, .store 11 7, .store 12 8]
/-- State reached by `w3o` (§57). -/
def w3 : LState := final K0 [] w3o
/-- State reached by `w3o` and `endUse` of the structure (§57). -/
def w3e : LState := final K0 [] (w3o ++ [.endUse 5])
/-- Run of W3 with the blocks issued into fields of the structure (§77, §60, §65): structure 2
with the fields 3 to 8; storage 9 (leaves 10, 11, 12), `internal` 3; blocks 4, 5, 6 issued into
the fields 3, 4, 5; views 7, 8, 9 derived from them and stored into the fields 6, 7, 8. -/
def w3vo : List Op := [.enter [] [lf, lf, lf, pt 2, pt 2, pt 2, pt 2, pt 2, pt 2], .write 1 [1],
  .alloc 1 0 [lf, pt 9, pt 9, pt 9], .write 0 [0], .newArena 9 3, .issue 0 [10] 3,
  .issue 0 [11] 4, .issue 0 [12] 5, .derive 4 [10] .observe, .derive 5 [11] .observe,
  .derive 6 [12] .observe, .store 7 6, .store 8 7, .store 9 8]
/-- State reached by `w3vo` (§57). -/
def w3v : LState := final K0 [] w3vo

/-- **W3** (material §5b, frame arena; class Lib, not given by the material). `alloc`,
`newArena`, three `issue`, three views stored into a local structure; `reset` while the views
live; `endUse` of the structure; `reset`; reissue. Expected (material): `reset` during the views
`reject`; after `endUse` of the structure `ok`; reissue `ok`. Obtained, literal reading (blocks
issued to the locals 2, 3, 4): `reject` during the views (§78.2); after `endUse` of the structure,
`reset` is still `reject`, the three blocks being held by the values 2, 3, 4 (§78.2); after their
end, `reset` and the reissue are `ok`. With the blocks issued into fields of the structure: the
expected verdicts (§78.2, §69 effect, §77). **MISMATCH** on the literal reading (after `endUse`
of the structure: expected `ok`, obtained `reject`); cause: case defect, the material does not say
which values hold the blocks.
STMT: : RunsTo K0 [] w3o w3 ∧ ResetD 0 w3 .reject ∧
    RunsTo K0 [] (w3o ++ [.endUse 5]) w3e ∧ ResetD 0 w3e .reject ∧
    Runs K0 [] (w3o ++ [.endUse 5, .endUse 2, .endUse 3, .endUse 4, .reset 0, .issue 0 [10] 2]) ∧
    RunsTo K0 [] w3vo w3v ∧ ResetD 0 w3v .reject ∧
    Runs K0 [] (w3vo ++ [.endUse 2, .reset 0, .issue 0 [10] 3])

# Task brief (verbatim obligations, as given by the user)

Normative hierarchy: Charter v0 highest (contradictions reported, never resolved); spec specs/ERN_Memory_Model_Specification_v0.md validated and frozen, cite by section; draft branches formal/* are material only (reuse when matching the spec, divergences resolved in favor of the spec and listed).
Layout (suggested): Ern/MemoryModel/Machine.lean (Part III), Ern/MemoryModel/Access/*.lean (Parts IV-XIII, XV-XVI), Ern/MemoryModel/Arena.lean (Part XIV: arenas as reference library abstraction; O17-O19 derived over O1-O16 plus metadata; ArenaInv and the §56 guard as abstraction contract), Ern/MemoryModel/Refinement.lean (§82), Ern/Lib/HandlePool.lean, Ern/Lib/DataStack.lean (non-normative), test modules imported by no model module. MM-01 (Part II) referenced, not a module.

Obligations (all mandatory):
1. Machine (Part III). Relations total and deterministic; interpreters calculable with static obligations and WF as proof arguments; agreement theorems both ways on their domain; admissible-state invariants preserved; P1-P4, no double free, frame lemmas, read-after-write on every included sub-range (§16).
2. Kernel (Parts IV-XIII). Every operation exactly as written, including §63.8 and §77 local self-blocking prevention, §65 store rules (derived authority, free leaf, arrival-state exercisability), §72 parameter-origin rule, §73 reanchoring to the first surviving active origin, §69/§70 end of use and free, pinning rules. Locals created by entering a frame are owned directly by the frame; alloc creates exactly one root. Theorems: preservation of WF3 ∧ Inv3 ∧ AnchorOrderHeld ∧ NoOrphan by every step; reachable invariant from S3.init statics under DDSound; exitFrame_no_dangling; call_params_effective_protected; effective_exclusive; init_only_by_writes, init_statics, and the global induction (every Init leaf of a reached state was declared or written); correspondence between Step and Reachable.
3. Arena (Part XIV). issue_as_kernel, reset_as_kernel (both directions, same arrival state on the kernel part), newArena_as_library (no safety property depends on the guard), arena_reuse_safe, ArenaInv preserved.
4. Refinement (§82). Repr including MM-02 WF; R1, R2, R4, R6 for every kernel operation and derived arena operation; simulation with parameters fixed once per run; freeSound_derived; pinned_address_stable; exclusive_bytes. Decisions to apply: declared disjointness is disjointness of leaves (byte disjointness follows from layout well-formedness); a pointer to an empty region has address = base of the effective anchor's allocation and that allocation as provenance; a region's pointer address is the lowest address among its non-empty leaves; a leaf receiving a reference has pointer size (stated hypothesis, classed types/ABI).
5. HandlePool (contract: v0.4 annex). Composite borrow (companion derived from internal over the whole storage, entries derived from the companion); resolveMany Observe by Observe derivations, distinctness only in Modify; allocSlot/freeSlot require a live pool and Modify on the pool value; newPool requires Uninit storage; freeSlot ends the entry content with endUse effects, preconditions excluding internal and its ancestors; PoolInv = entry disjointness + pool_no_stale_access + transition guarantee that freeSlot never succeeds on an entry covered by an active companion descendant. Theorems: pool_resolve_modify_exclusive, pool_no_stale_access, stale/other-pool/atomicity/distinctness, pool_freeSlot_ends_content under the Modify right.
6. DataStack (contract below, identifier DS-v1). Marks carry stack identity and a fresh mark identifier; the stack keeps the ordered list of live marks; rewind m fails on a dead or foreign mark, rejects if an active authority derived from internal covers a cell above m, otherwise returns those cells to available and removes m and every mark above it; push and grow use the derived issue; grow is in place only (same base, extension into the space directly after the block, fail otherwise). Theorems: rewind_rejects_live_above, mark_no_aba (for every removed mark), rewind_keeps_older_marks, grow_same_base, grow_keeps_prefix_init, grow_keeps_prefix_bytes through the refinement.
7. Corpora. Encode MM2-H (first execution), MM3-H and MM23-H (replay) from the attached material, plus new cases: §63.8 and §77 self-blocking (reject, with twins), §56 guard, corrected HandlePool, DataStack (including ABA and a multi-stack frame scenario), W1-W3. Each case: reached state from the initial state, expected verdict from its source, positive twin for each rejection, class. MM23-H15 and H16 must now pass. Section J of MM3-H stays unencoded and classified. No case is corrected or bypassed.

Docstrings: model modules: every def/theorem cites the specification clause it formalizes. Library modules: cite the applicable spec clauses (§36, §56, ...) and the local contract identifier (HandlePool v0.4 annex, DS-v1), stated as non-normative.
Exclusions: instrumented checked variants; duplicate _pre statements; references to draft reports; concurrency beyond the stat boundary; syntax.
Rules: zero sorry; #print axioms at most {propext, Quot.sound} on every constant (checked by script); no noncomputable; lake build without warnings; nothing invented - a clause that cannot be formalized as written is reported, not interpreted; no statement weakened relative to its clause; adversarial review rounds, every finding re-checked by a refuter.
Opening the PR: only if every mandatory obligation is proved and every expected/obtained mismatch resolved; otherwise commit on the branch, do not push, do not open the PR, end with a blocking report (each unproved obligation or mismatch classified as specification defect, module defect or case defect, with its counterexample). Never present a partial formalization as conforming.

===== H04
**MM23-H04** (material §3, class R). Transfer of a value in place. Expected (material): a read then a write of the bytes, provenance kept; the source `Moved` and unreadable, its bytes still initialized. Obtained: the same. From the reached state of H03, the raw operations of `transfer(v, w)` are a read of the range of `v` then a write of the range of `w` (§82, §63); after them the range of `w` holds the bytes of `v`, value and provenance (§16 ¶2, §20.2 ¶1), and the range of `v` is unchanged and initialized; in the kernel the leaf of `v` is `Moved` (§63 effect) and every read of it is rejected (§66.1). Twin of the rejected read, the same run without the transfer: the read of `v` is `ok`. The provenance is kept because the realization writes the bytes it read, provenance included (§16 ¶2, §20.2 ¶1); propagation of provenance through copies is not fixed by spec v0 at the level of the language (§10 ¶4, §19): open obligation, not a mismatch.
===== H09
The raw operations realizing the exit of frame 1 in R1 (§82, §73). -/ def x1 : List (Machine.Op Unit) := opsOf π1 .exit (st1 9).1 (st1 9).2 /-- **MM23-H09** (material §3, class R). Frame exit. Expected (material): one deallocation per automatic allocation, none for the owned storage. Obtained: the same for the realization of the reference (`exitOps`): after nine steps of R1 (reached), the exit is realized by one `ok` deallocation of the allocation of each root local 0, 1, 2 of the frame with its recorded token (§17, §82.5), dead afterwards, and none for the storage 3, live afterwards. **Source gap (open obligation)**: spec v0 does not require the first half: §9 ¶2 ("storage with static or automatic duration, whose particular rules will be defined later") and §73 ("Exiting does not entail automatic physical deallocation of all dead places") leave the deallocation of automatic storage at exit undetermined; it is a choice of the realization, not a spec v0 guarantee.
===== H02
Contract of R2 (§48, §70.2): the storage 4 and the block region leaf 5 deallocable with the authority 104, so that only the structural clause of `free` can reject. -/ abbrev K2 : K := KT { dealloc := [4, 5], compat := [(4, 104), (5, 104)] } false true /-- Run R2 (§72, §67, §71, §76, §77, §63, §66, §69, §78): frame 1 with the arena value 0, the provider 1, the values `v` (2) and `q` (3); storage 4 (leaves 5, 6) owned by 0, its root authority 4 the `internal` of the arena; block 5 on `[5]` issued to `v` (the reference to leaf 5 written into `v`); leaf 5 written through block 5; `transfer(v, q)`; `read(q)`; `endUse(q)`; `reset`. -/ def l2 : List LOp := [.kernel (.enter [] [lf, lf, lf, lf]), .kernel (.write 1 [1] wv), .kernel (.alloc 1 0 [lf, pt 4, pt 4]), .kernel (.write 0 [0] wv), .newArena [] 4 4, .issue 0 [5] 2, .kernel (.write 5 [5] wv), .kernel (.transfer 2 3), .kernel (.read 3 [3]), .kernel (.endUse 3), .reset 0] /-- Parameters of R2, fixed once from its final places (§82). -/ def π2 : Params Unit := piOf (placesOf [] l2) [] /-- State of R2 after its first `n` steps (§82.7). -/ def lt2 (n : Nat) : LState × Machine.State := lfin K2 [] π2 (l2.take n) /-- The arena entry of R2 before the reset (§46): storage 4, `internal` 4, leaf 6 available, block 5 issued on `[5]`. -/ def E2 : ArenaEntry := ⟨4, 4, [6], [([5], 5)]⟩ /-- The library state after the `reset` of R2 (§78), as computed by the corpus runner. -/ def l2r : LState := next K2 (lt2 10).1 (.reset 0) /-- **MM23-H02** (material §3, class R). `reset` of an arena, then access through an old block authority. Expected (material): no safe program reaches it; the memory machine would accept it (the allocation is live). Obtained: the same. R2 is reached up to the end of `q` and through the `reset` (`LSim`); the `reset` is `ok` (§78) and its state library-reachable; block 5 is inactive there and a read through it is rejected (§66.2); along every continuation of the library run, no kernel step uses block 5 (`reset_no_access`, §82.7, §78, §86: no step reactivates an authority). In the memory machine the allocation of the storage is live, the range of leaf 5 still holds the bytes written through block 5, and a raw read of it is `ok`. Twin of the rejected read, the same run without the end of the block and the `reset`: the read through block 5 is `ok`. The draft lemma stating that no authority derived from `internal` remains active after `reset` is false under spec v0 (§78 effect: "an empty-footprint derivative may remain active"); the statement used is restricted to authorities covering a leaf of the storage (§78.2).
===== H13
**MM23-H13** (material §3, class R). A value containing a pointer, transferred then read. Expected (material): provenance kept. Obtained: the same. On R2 (reached before the transfer, after it and after the read), the derived `issue` wrote into `v` the reference to leaf 5: it decodes to the address of leaf 5, every byte with the provenance of the storage allocation (§82.3); after `transfer(v, q)` the range of `q` holds the same bytes (§63, §16 ¶2); `read(q)` is `ok` in the kernel, realized by one raw read of the range of `q`, `ok`, which returns the bytes written into `v`, provenance included, and they decode to the address of leaf 5 (§20.2 ¶1, §82.2). No rejection, no twin. As in H04, the copy keeps provenance by the choice of the realization; propagation through copies stays open in spec v0 (§10 ¶4, §19).
===== H15
Contract of R5 and R6 (§48): nothing declared. -/ abbrev K5 : K := KT {} false true /-- Run R5 (§72, §67, §71, §76, §77, §61, §65): frame 1 with the arena value 0, the provider 1, the leaves 2, 3, 4; storage 5 (leaf 6) owned by 0, its root authority 5 the `internal` of the arena; the derived `issue` of the empty region to 2 (block 6: `split` of 5 into `[[]]`, then `store` into 2); `split` of the root of 3 into `[[]]` (authority 7), then `store` of 7 into 4. -/ def l5 : List LOp := [.kernel (.enter [] [lf, lf, lf, lf, lf]), .kernel (.write 1 [1] wv), .kernel (.alloc 1 0 [lf, pt 5]), .kernel (.write 0 [0] wv), .newArena [] 5 5, .issue 0 [] 2, .kernel (.split 3 [[]]), .kernel (.store 7 4)] /-- Parameters of R5, fixed once from its final places (§82). -/ def π5 : Params Unit := piOf (placesOf [] l5) [] /-- State of R5 after its first `n` steps (§82.7). -/ def lt5 (n : Nat) : LState × Machine.State := lfin K5 [] π5 (l5.take n) /-- **MM23-H15** (material §3, class R). Reference to an empty region, by `issue []` and by `split` into `[]` then `store`. Expected (material): address the base of the allocation of the effective anchor; provenance that allocation. Obtained: the same; the case passes. R5 is reached (`LSim`), the issue being the derived library operation: its raw operations are one write, of the destination 2 (`split` realizes none, §77, §82.7). Block 6 has the empty region, effective anchor 5 (the root of the storage), recorded in the arena entry; the range of 2 decodes to the base of the allocation of 5, nonzero, every byte with that allocation as provenance. Authority 7 has the empty region, effective anchor 3; the range of 4 decodes to the base of the allocation of 3, nonzero, with that provenance. Both destinations have the size of a reference (8 bytes). Source of the expected verdict: a decision of the brief recorded for §82.3 (empty-region rule), not stated by spec v0 (§81 leaves encodings to Spec 11).
===== H16
Run R6 (§72, §67, §71, §76, §77): frame 1 with the arena value 0, the provider 1, the leaf 2; storage 3 (leaves 4 at offset 0 and 5 at offset 8) owned by 0, its root authority 3 the `internal` of the arena; the derived `issue` of the region `[5, 4]` to 2 (block 4). -/ def l6 : List LOp := [.kernel (.enter [] [lf, lf, lf]), .kernel (.write 1 [1] wv), .kernel (.alloc 1 0 [lf, pt 3, pt 3]), .kernel (.write 0 [0] wv), .newArena [] 3 3, .issue 0 [5, 4] 2] /-- Parameters of R6, fixed once from its final places (§82). -/ def π6 : Params Unit := piOf (placesOf [] l6) [] /-- State of R6 after its first `n` steps (§82.7). -/ def lt6 (n : Nat) : LState × Machine.State := lfin K5 [] π6 (l6.take n) /-- **MM23-H16** (material §3, class R). Reference to a region whose first listed leaf does not have the lowest offset. Expected (material): the lowest address among the nonempty leaves. Obtained: the same; the case passes. R6 is reached (`LSim`), the issue being the derived library operation, realized by one write of the destination 2. Block 4 has the region `[5, 4]`, recorded in the arena entry; both leaves have nonzero size, leaf 4 at offset 0 below the head 5 at offset 8; the range of 2 decodes to the address of leaf 4, not to that of the head, every byte with the storage allocation as provenance. Source of the expected verdict: a decision of the brief recorded for §82.3 (lowest-address rule), not stated by spec v0 (§81).
